description:
Elixir reads an attribute by one rule: @name followed by an expression. fz's front door (parse_attribute_item) accepts only @doc/@moduledoc followed by a string literal, plus @spec and @type. The surface (parse_scope_attr, quoted_function) decodes only those names, and everything else is 'unsupported attribute head'.

Under the one rule:
- A value attribute ('@read_ahead_size 64 * 1024') is read back as @read_ahead_size in function bodies. Seen writing lib/option_parser.fz (fz-sc8.16), and fz-mue's integration fixture 01860 reads @nums, @strs and @ws in bodies (lines 1806-1849).
- @compile {:inline, [...]} is a value attribute that nothing reads. It spans 6 lines in fixture 01860. Folded from fz-mue.13 (reproducer /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-otp-json/punch/23_compile_attr.fz).
- @moduledoc false (and @doc false) is the doc attribute taking a value that is not a string. Folded from fz-mue.14 (reproducer /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-otp-json/punch/40_moduledoc_none.fz).
- Library code that inlined a constant for want of attributes is folded back onto an attribute.

Done when: a fixture on all three paths reads value attributes in bodies, and the punch/23 and punch/40 reproducers compile.

The multi-line @spec half of the old description moved to fz-mue.15 (type attributes read to the end of their expression). Re-cut agreed by Elixir Parity, which builds both; one PR each, stacked.

title: A module attribute is @name followed by an expression
